findings.text: The report's closing prose states 'No committed figure was re-rendered in this node; the four below are the committed PNG paths a later regeneration wave must rewrite once a solve is run', but the bullet list it introduces carries six PNG paths and the report's own table sums to six (certificate-ladder 4 + repaired-remeasure-receipt 1 + repaired-remeasure 1). The run's manifest follow_ons and the evidence fragment both say six, so the fragment and the report disagree on the count and the report contradicts its own table. The paths themselves are all correct and present; only the number 'four' is wrong.

The after arm was independently reproduced by the review at the reviewed head 1a6645424 in the reviewed worktree: 11 passed in 91.64 s EXIT=0 (logs/review_head_suite.log under the reviewing run directory); the negative control was independently reproduced too - base blobs of the three drivers at 68762d363 give EXIT=1 listing the same four sites (logs/review_base_scan.log); head arm (logs/review_head_scan.log) gives EXIT=0.

justifications.durability: The guard demonstrably fires rather than merely passing: reverting the change (base blobs) makes the scanner exit 1 with the four sites, and applying it makes it exit 0, which I reproduced independently. The fix uses the optional parameter the painter already documents for exactly this purpose, so it carries no new mechanism to rot. Weaknesses keeping this off full marks. No committed test pins these three drivers: tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py exercises the scanner against synthetic corpora and one unrelated renderer (root-cause/closed-forms/render.py), so a future edit that drops wall=wall from any of the four sites reddens nothing in the repo suite - the regression guard is the manual per-batch scanner run, which matches the design of this audit but leaves the fix unpinned in CI. And the committed PNGs remain stale: the renders were not regenerated (correctly per this node's instruction not to re-render), so the on-disk figures still show the unmasked field until the declared regeneration wave runs the solves.
justifications.evidence: Every headline was reproduced first-hand. Head gate: tests/renderer_wall_scan.py over the three drivers, EXIT=0 at the reviewed head in the reviewed worktree. Negative control reproduced independently rather than taken from the log: I extracted the three measure.py blobs at base 68762d363 into a scratch tree under $TMPDIR and ran the same scanner, which exits 1 and lists exactly the four sites with their base line numbers - byte-for-byte the same set the run recorded in base_scan.log. Suite: tests/test_renderer_wall_scan.py passes 11 in both arms, and I reran the head arm (11 passed in 118.55 s, EXIT=0). The run's manifest declares real, non-empty baseline_suite and after_suite objects with log paths, both completed true. Deduction: the committed report's closing prose reads 'the four below are the committed PNG paths a later regeneration wave must rewrite' while the list beneath it carries six paths and the run's own table and fragment both say six - a reader reconciling the report against its own bullets cannot make the count agree (finding 1).
justifications.fit: Minimal and idiomatic. The change is four additions of one existing keyword to existing calls, using the painter's documented wall parameter; no new dependency, no new abstraction, no refactor, and nothing introduced beyond what the goal requires. The same fix is applied uniformly at the four sites, and no surrounding code is touched. Deductions are minor and shared with the evidence/durability dimensions (the report numeric slip, the manual-only regression guard), not with the shape of the change.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The reviewed run's goal - route every unguarded scattered-field renderer call in this batch through the wall mask - is met and independently reproduced. The single commit 1a6645424 adds wall=wall to exactly the four draw_flux_contours calls the base scanner lists (certificate-ladder-500-1000-probe/measure.py:113 and :133, repaired-remeasure-receipt/measure.py:70, repaired-remeasure/measure.py:70). I reproduced the head gate independently in the reviewed worktree: tests/renderer_wall_scan.py over the three drivers exits 0. I confirmed the wall object at each site is context['machine'].wall_node, the same array the driver already hands to certificate._raster_field and poloidal.draw_wall, so the mask is applied to the raster the driver actually renders - not a mismatched or empty wall. All four calls were already unfilled line-contour draws on stated level arrays, so no filled contour is introduced. Not full marks only for a report-side numeric slip (finding 1), not for the change itself.
justifications.scope_discipline: The review range 68762d363..1a6645424 touches exactly four repository paths - docs/figures/centroid-constrained-oracle-solve/{certificate-ladder-500-1000-probe,repaired-remeasure-receipt,repaired-remeasure}/measure.py and docs/figures/../fsa-wall-mask-centroid-drivers.html - all four inside the run's granted write paths, plus the out-of-repo report under the grant. No product source under nova/ is edited, no plan, shared index, or concurrent-node path is touched, and the three same-named drivers are edited without collision. The single commit carries a conventional subject and an explanatory body; a trailer scan is clean and a label/naming scan over the four changed paths finds no plan/stage/ticket identifier. The change is read-only with respect to behaviour beyond the argument: it adds one keyword to calls that already existed.
